title: Taking up the guitar at seven
summary: The house had a piano, guitar and drums; he picked up the guitar by ear and liked its sound.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: You started playing guitar about nine years old, something like that?
I was playing guitar at seven.
About seven?
Yeah.
What's your first memory of the guitar? Why the guitar? Why did you pick the guitar out?
Well, there was a piano in the house and a guitar and drums.
Uh-huh.
So I took the guitar.
How come there was instruments around?
Your parents were musicians?
My parents liked to fool around with them.
Uh-huh.
And every time we tried to give a little
party at the house we all get these instruments together and tried to play them. So I took the guitar.
Relatives and so forth.
Yeah. The rest of them got the other stuff.
Was it hearing somebody else play the guitar that made you pick it, or --
No. I just picked it up.
Just picked it up.
From just what I heard.
You liked the sound of it?
I liked the sound of it.
Uh-huh.
That's why I stuck to it.
Could anybody in your family play very well?
My mother couldn't. My father played a mandolin.
Uh-huh.
My mother played a little bit of piano.
Right.
Christians, you know. They were Christians.
Church music?
Yeah. Church music.
Did he play the mandolin in the
My father did.
Yeah. Right. And they had a guitar, huh?
And they had a guitar and I picked up the guitar and I just taught myself. Wasn't so hard for me to play it either, because I just picked it up and started playing it, from hearing the music.
You just found the notes.
Yeah. I just found the notes, picked it up.
